_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Palau covering Micronesian settlement (~3000 BCE, among oldest in Pacific), megalithic terraces (Babeldaob), stone village platforms, Spanish claim (1574), German purchase (1899), Japanese mandate (1914-44, Nanyo-cho, major development, Japanese population exceeded Palauans), WWII (Battle of Peleliu 1944, bloodiest per capita), US Trust Territory (1947-1994), nuclear-free constitution (unique, delayed independence), Compact of Free Association 1994, marine sanctuary.

country_profile.government_type: Unitary presidential republic in free association with the United States

population.source: Palau Bureau of Budget and Planning

religion.note: Catholic (Spanish/German missionaries, largest single denomination); Evangelical (Liebenzell Mission, German); Seventh-day Adventist; Latter-day Saints; Modekngei (indigenous syncretic religion, blend of Christianity and traditional beliefs, founded early 1900s as resistance to foreign religion, unique to Palau); traditional beliefs (chelid spirits, taboo system, bai meeting house spiritual significance)

ethnic_groups.name: Palauan
ethnic_groups.notes: Micronesian/Melanesian mixed ancestry; matrilineal (women control land and money, clan mothers select chiefs, unique in Pacific); bai (traditional meeting house, elaborate storyboard carvings, UNESCO); stone money connection (Yapese quarried limestone from Palau, historical trade); complex ranked clan system; betel nut (buuch, universal social custom); traditional fishing/taro culture; first-born women hold special economic/political power

ethnic_groups.name: Filipino
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest foreign group; construction/service workers; labour migration; economically important; some integration issues

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese
ethnic_groups.notes: Business community; PRC nationals; construction; commercial shops; tourism industry

ethnic_groups.name: Other Asian
ethnic_groups.notes: Bangladeshi (construction workers); Vietnamese; Japanese (legacy community, Japanese period 1914-44, Japanese population once exceeded Palauans, cultural influences remain: food, words, customs)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Carolinian (outer island Micronesians, Sonsorolese/Tobian, distinct cultures); American (military, advisors); Micronesian (Chuukese, Yapese); European; mixed heritage common

independence.from: US Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (Compact of Free Association; US handles defence, citizens can live/work in US; last Trust Territory entity to gain independence)

country_profile.notes_unique: Battle of Peleliu (September-November 1944, US Marines vs Japanese, 2 months, 10,695 US casualties including 1,794 dead, ~11,000 Japanese killed of 11,000, one of bloodiest Pacific battles, Bloody Nose Ridge, coral caves, questionable strategic necessity); Nuclear-free constitution (1979, world's first nuclear-free constitution, required 75% referendum to override, 7 referendums failed before amendment allowed COFA with US nuclear transit, delayed independence by 15 years); Palau National Marine Sanctuary (2015, 80% of EEZ protected, 500,000 km² no-take zone, one of world's largest, marine conservation leader); Rock Islands Southern Lagoon (UNESCO World Heritage, 445 uninhabited limestone islands, Jellyfish Lake/Ongeim'l Tketau with millions of golden jellyfish that lost stingers through evolution, unique); matrilineal society (women control land/clan resources, clan mothers choose chiefs, women central to political decisions, bul system of conservation, unique in Micronesia); Babeldaob (largest island, megalithic terraces/earthworks among largest ancient structures in Pacific, pre-European, purpose debated); Japanese legacy (1914-44, Koror developed as administrative centre, Japanese population outnumbered Palauans 4:1 by 1940, cultural influences persist: food/bento, words, infrastructure, Shinto shrines remnants); Compact of Free Association (COFA, 1994 last Trust Territory, renewed, US military access, citizens can live in US); diving (world-class, Blue Corner, German Channel, shipwrecks, manta rays); small population (18k, one of smallest UN member states); storyboards (bai house carved panels depicting legends, valuable art form); bul (traditional moratorium on fishing areas, indigenous conservation, inspired modern marine policies)

current_leader.notes: Independent; businessman; pro-Taiwan (strong, invited Tsai Ing-wen to visit); marine conservation; COFA renewal focus; US alliance; tourism recovery post-COVID; China diplomatic pressure resistance

former_leaders.notes: Longest-serving; marine sanctuary 2015 (signature achievement, 80% EEZ protected); climate champion; 'ocean president'; Taiwan ally; four terms total

former_leaders.name: Johnson Toribiong
former_leaders.notes: Lawyer; maintained Taiwan ties; infrastructure projects; one term

former_leaders.name: Kuniwo Nakamura
former_leaders.notes: First elected president under COFA; Compact Capital construction (Ngerulmud, moved capital from Koror to Babeldaob 2006); nation building

former_leaders.name: Haruo Remeliik
former_leaders.notes: First president of Republic of Palau (self-governing 1981); assassinated 1985 (shot, politically motivated, nuclear constitution disputes); founding father; tragic death
